scenario: [LDET.3.2.7] the canonical Float text form on the JSON data plane. A finite Float serializes to the shortest decimal that reparses to the identical IEEE-754 double, shaped like the compiler's lowering of a Float literal ([LUNI.2.7]): bare %g (6 sig-figs) would render 3.141592653589793 as "3.14159" and fail, and a whole Float keeps its ".0" — 42.0 serializes to "42.0", never "42" ("42" reparses as an Int, silently collapsing the value's kind, FINDING §1). The raw JSON text is pinned via value_json so the Float->Int collapse is caught; a parsed-number compare (value) cannot tell "42" from "42.0". A non-finite Float is the separate case A7 folds in here: Inf is a valid working-memory value (it asserts fine — only NaN is rejected, LEXP.4.2), but "inf" is not valid JSON, so an Inf cache value is a NOT_REPRESENTABLE trap at the verb (LDET.3.2.7_a_nonfinite_cache_value_is_a_trap; ds.json.nonfinite_total{verb=cache}) and the write is suppressed rather than emitting a corrupt token. This fixture asserts three finite values (full-precision irrational, the whole float 42.0, the 17-digit 0.1+0.2 sum) with an Inf between them: the Inf produces no cache_set, and the finite value after it still serializes — proving the guard is non-finite-only and the engine recovers.

schema Trig scope ttl 1_h:
    v: Float

rule r:
    Trig t
->
    cache key: "k" value: t.v
